knowledge:
- key_parameters: spike=A DataFrame containing spike-in sequence database details (methylation status, CpG count, GC fraction, etc.) loaded via data(spike) or custom-built ;; bsgenome=Character string specifying the BSgenome package to load (e.g., "BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38") for genomic bias adjustment ;; ret=Return format for predict_pmol(), set to "df" to return a data frame ;; genome=Genome build identifier (e.g., "hg38") used in scan_genomic_bedpe()
- alternatives: None mentioned. The package supports either BAM or BEDPE formats for input.
- when_to_use: When performing absolute quantification of cell-free methylated DNA from cfMeDIP-seq experiments that utilize synthetic spike-in controls to adjust for PCR and immunoprecipitation biases.
- pitfalls: If methylation specificity calculated by methylation_specificity() is < 0.98, the cfMeDIP experiment performed inadequately and the sample should be flagged or removed ;; BAM files must be indexed (using samtools index) ;; BEDPE files must be sorted, compressed with bgzip, and indexed with tabix ;; Contig name mismatches between BAM/BEDPE files and the spike database can occur, resulting in warnings.

workflows.name: cfmedip_quant_bam
workflows.intent: Perform absolute quantification and bias adjustment of cfMeDIP-seq data using BAM input files.
workflows.stages: 1. Load spike-in database ;; 2. Scan genomic BAM to get genomic coverage ;; 3. Scan spike-in BAM to get spike coverage ;; 4. Calculate methylation specificity ;; 5. Fit Gaussian GLM on spike-in data ;; 6. Predict molar concentration (pmol) for genomic regions ;; 7. Bin and adjust molar concentration into genomic windows
workflows.code:
data(spike)
genomic_bam_path <- system.file("extdata", "example_chr21.bam", package="spiky", mustWork=TRUE)
genomic_coverage <- scan_genomic_contigs(genomic_bam_path,spike=spike)
spike_bam_path <- system.file("extdata", "example.spike.bam", package="spiky", mustWork=TRUE)
spikes_coverage <- scan_spike_contigs(spike_bam_path,spike=spike)
methyl_spec <- methylation_specificity(spikes_coverage,spike=spike)
print(methyl_spec)
gaussian_glm <- model_glm_pmol(spikes_coverage,spike=spike)
summary(gaussian_glm)
sample_data_pmol <- predict_pmol(gaussian_glm, genomic_coverage,bsgenome="BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38",ret="df")
head(sample_data_pmol,n=1)
sample_binned_data <- bin_pmol(sample_data_pmol)
head(sample_binned_data,n=1)

workflows.name: cfmedip_quant_bedpe
workflows.intent: Perform absolute quantification and bias adjustment of cfMeDIP-seq data using BEDPE input files.
input: genomic_bedpe.bed.gz (Sorted, bgzipped BEDPE file of genomic reads)
spike_bedpe.bed.gz (Sorted, bgzipped BEDPE file of spike-in reads)
workflows.stages: 1. Load spike-in database ;; 2. Scan genomic BEDPE to get genomic coverage ;; 3. Scan spike-in BEDPE to get spike coverage ;; 4. Calculate methylation specificity ;; 5. Fit Gaussian GLM on spike-in data ;; 6. Predict molar concentration (pmol) for genomic regions ;; 7. Bin and adjust molar concentration into genomic windows
workflows.code:
data(spike)
genomic_bedpe_path <- system.file("extdata", "example_chr21_bedpe.bed.gz", package="spiky", mustWork=TRUE)
genomic_coverage <- scan_genomic_bedpe(genomic_bedpe_path,genome="hg38")
spike_bedpe_path <- system.file("extdata", "example_spike_bedpe.bed.gz", package="spiky", mustWork=TRUE)
spikes_coverage <- scan_spike_bedpe(spike_bedpe_path,spike=spike)
methyl_spec <- methylation_specificity(spikes_coverage,spike=spike)
print(methyl_spec)
gaussian_glm <- model_glm_pmol(spikes_coverage,spike=spike)
summary(gaussian_glm)
sample_data_pmol <- predict_pmol(gaussian_glm, genomic_coverage,bsgenome="BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38",ret="df")
head(sample_data_pmol,n=1)
sample_binned_data <- bin_pmol(sample_data_pmol)
head(sample_binned_data,n=1)
